title: Random Three-Wire Permutation Pseudorandomness
summary: The broader random three-wire reversible-circuit conjecture remains open; the unresolved task is to determine whether polynomially many iterations yield pseudorandomness.

formal_statement.body: Let $P:\{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}^n$ be the randomized permutation process that chooses three random wires and applies a uniformly random permutation to those wires. The unresolved conjecture asks whether there is a polynomial $p$ such that the iterated process $P^{p(n)}$ is a pseudorandom permutation. This is the broader random three-wire reversible-circuit question; it is weaker than the preceding restricted conjectures, so refuting it would also refute those conjectures.

scope.domain: Random three-wire reversible circuits and pseudorandom permutations in symmetric cryptography.
parameters: n: bit-length of the permutation domain
three wires: number of randomly selected wires per step
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether there exists a polynomial p for which the iterated process P^{p(n)} is a pseudorandom permutation.

citations.label: When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness

progress.summary: The source labels this as Conjecture 7 and presents it as broader and weaker than the preceding restricted conjectures. It notes that refuting this conjecture would also refute those conjectures.
